Interpreting 'each' as a per-group quantity rather than a total
Counting rows and columns in a rectangular arrangement without recounting or omitting
Mapping a multiplication expression a x b onto a group count and a per-group count
Recognizing that a total can be produced by repeated addition of equal-sized groups

included: Fact families x2, x5, x10 with the other factor from 1 to 10
Single-step equal-groups word problems with explicit group count and per-group count
Arrays with up to 10 rows and up to 10 columns, presented visually
Translating between an array, an equal-groups picture, and a multiplication sentence
Skip-counting sequences by 2, 5, and 10 used as a solution strategy

assumptions.claim: Reina can execute equal-groups multiplication accurately when visual group outlines and a demonstration remain available, but this performance is support-dependent and does not yet indicate independent skill.
assumptions.uncertainty: The 90% figure comes from a single guided session; no unassisted equal-groups measurement exists, so the size of the support effect is unknown.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: An unassisted equal-groups probe on fresh items scoring at or near 90% would show the support was not load-bearing.

assumptions.claim: Independent array interpretation is currently below working level (40% on 5 unseen items).
assumptions.uncertainty: Five items is a very small sample; the confidence interval around 40% is wide and could plausibly span roughly 15%-70%.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: An independent array probe of 10 or more fresh items scoring above 70% would contradict the low estimate.

assumptions.claim: The gap between guided equal-groups accuracy and independent array accuracy is best explained by removal of support and by a groups-versus-per-group mapping confusion, rather than by an array-specific perceptual difficulty.
assumptions.uncertainty: Support removal and item type are confounded across the two observations; no probe has varied one while holding the other constant. The teacher note is second-hand and undated.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: An unassisted equal-groups probe at high accuracy paired with a supported array probe at low accuracy would locate the difficulty in array format rather than in support removal or the mapping confusion.

assumptions.claim: Reversal of group count and per-group count is a recurring error pattern that will surface in word-problem interpretation.
assumptions.uncertainty: Teacher-stream report only; no scored work item in the packet shows the reversal directly, and reversals often do not change the numeric answer, so they may be invisible in accuracy scores.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Work samples or think-aloud responses in which Reina consistently labels which number is the group count and which is the per-group count.

assumptions.claim: Skip-counting fluency by 2, 5, and 10 is untested in this packet and cannot be assumed as an available strategy.
assumptions.uncertainty: No academic evidence addresses skip counting at all; this assumption is a statement of absence, not a measured estimate.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Any timed or untimed skip-counting probe result, in either direction, replaces this assumption with data.

assumptions.claim: Session engagement has been high, but engagement evidence carries no information about mastery of any construct in this assignment.
assumptions.uncertainty: The wheel and pronunciation logs are low-confidence, drawn from spelling rather than math, and show four initiations against two completions; no stable preference or disposition can be inferred.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Not applicable to mastery claims; this assumption exists only to bar engagement data from academic inference.

planningRationale: The packet contains one internally contradictory pair: supported equal-groups performance at 90% (academic:guided-groups) against independent array performance at 40% (academic:independent-array). These two observations differ on two dimensions at once, support level and item format, so neither alone explains the gap. teacher:group-reversal offers a third candidate explanation, a groups-versus-per-group mapping confusion, but is teacher-stream and unscored. The plan therefore opens with an unassisted mixed-construct probe that varies format while holding support constant at zero, which is the smallest manipulation that can separate the three explanations. Instruction (node-02, node-03) is deliberately narrow and targets only the mapping distinction and the array-to-groups link, since these are the only mechanisms the evidence implicates; broader fact-family work is excluded by the difficulty boundaries. Guided practice logs support requests per item so assisted and unassisted performance never merge. No mastery claim is available anywhere in this sequence: the packet has no returned graded work and no delayed measurement, so node-05 and node-06 plus a returned artifact are all required before readiness is discussed. Skip counting is included as a probe target despite having zero supporting evidence precisely because that absence is itself a gap in the prerequisite chain. Engagement records are held entirely outside academic inference; the high fun rating, the completed pronunciation sessions, and the wheel likes describe session behavior and support no statement about what Reina knows, prefers, or can do.
